title: Fabricate a rigid line with a flare and a bend
subject: General
assumptions: The box is rated for at least the intended test pressure of 1.5 times system pressure.
Oblique close-up of one formed bend showing the outer and inner radius surfaces, taken so wrinkles, kinks or flat spots would cast visible shadow.

Measured record of flare geometry and bend deformation: the included flare angle at each end, the original tube OD, and the smallest diameter measured across each flattened bend expressed as a percentage of original OD.

Record of the pressure test: computed test pressure with the source of the system operating pressure, the peak gauge reading, and the observed hold with no decay and no seepage at either B-nut, either sleeve base, or the tube body.
openQuestions: Every check, error mode and evidence item in this pack was drafted by packs/compile_pack.py from the procedure sheet and handbook, and has not been reviewed by a subject-matter expert.

The procedure sheet specifies a 47° flare and a 47° die; the cited handbook page 9-4 says the aircraft flaring tool produces "a flare of 35° to 37°" and that an automotive tool producing 45° is impermissible. An SME must resolve which angle the assessment accepts before this pack is used.
Does the blue-sleeve-ring check depend on a specific sleeve finish? It fails as a criterion if the shop stocks unpainted or differently coloured sleeves.
The pressure test has no specified hold duration or allowable gauge decay; a number is needed for 'holds without decay' to be checkable.

Is a double flare required? Handbook p. 9-5 states a double flare is used on soft aluminium alloy tubing 3/8" OD and under, which would cover the 0.25" example stock; the procedure sheet teaches a single flare only.
Which document supplies the system operating pressure used to compute test pressure for this training article, and is it recorded on the worksheet?

steps.text: Use the safety wire method to map tubing length and bends.

checks.text: Both ends of the safety wire are seated into their respective fittings, with the wire spanning the complete route.
checks.src: Sheet: insert one end into the first fitting, route to the second, cut excess 'to allow it to feed into the other fitting'.

checks.text: Felt-tip marks are present on the wire at each bend location and at both fitting ends.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Use a marker to mark the location of each bend and ends.'

checks.text: The wire path clears surrounding structure and components rather than cutting through an obstruction.
checks.src: Sheet: route 'taking the most appropriate route'; routing done 'to avoid obstructions and excessive material waste'.

checks.text: No bend in the mapped wire route is tighter than the standard bend radius for the tube size selected.
checks.src: Handbook: 'Figure 9-4 shows preferred methods and standard bend radii for bending tubing by tube size.' Radius requires measurement against the table.

errors.text: Wire ends are not fed fully into the fittings, so the mapped length is short and the finished line will not reach.
Bend locations are not marked before the wire is removed, leaving bend positions unrecoverable.
Wire is routed by the shortest path through structure instead of a clear, installable route.

steps.text: Carefully remove the wire, keeping its shape.

checks.text: The removed wire still holds the routed contour, with every bend at the same angle and location as when installed.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Carefully remove the wire, keeping its shape" — shape is the template for bend locations.

checks.text: All felt-tip marks for the bend locations and both wire ends remain present and legible after removal.
checks.src: Routing note requires marking "the location of each bend and ends"; marks must survive to transfer to tubing.

checks.text: A drawing or photograph of the wire's shape exists as a record before the wire is further handled.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 2: "Draw or photograph the shape to make."

checks.text: The removed wire's shape still corresponds to a clear route between the two fittings without obstruction contact.
checks.src: Only verifiable by observing removal against the actual routing; a still of the wire alone cannot confirm the route.

errors.text: Wire is pulled straight or its bends are opened during removal, so bend locations and added length are wrong while the wire still looks usable.
Bend and end marks are smeared or rubbed off during removal, leaving no transferable dimensions.
No sketch or photograph of the shape is made before the wire is straightened for measuring.

steps.text: Straighten the wire and measure the total length.

checks.text: The safety wire is fully straightened, with no residual bows, kinks or curls remaining along its length.
checks.src: Step 3 requires the wire be straightened before measuring; residual curvature understates the routed length.

checks.text: The measured straightened-wire length matches the tape/scale reading recorded on the worksheet.
checks.src: Senior note: 'Use a tape measure for length'; the reading itself must be taken, not seen.

checks.text: The recorded tubing length equals the wire length plus 1/2 inch for each marked bend.
checks.src: Senior note: 'add 1/2" per bend. This is the length of tubing you will need.' Handbook states no per-bend figure.

checks.text: The recorded length includes extra material for bending variation rather than being the bare routed dimension.
checks.src: Handbook: 'cut approximately 10 percent longer than the tube to be replaced to provide for minor variations in bending.'

errors.text: Wire measured while still bowed or kinked, yielding a short length and a tube later strained into position.
Bend allowance omitted or applied once instead of per bend, so the tubing is cut too short.
Length recorded without units, or transcribed from the tape incorrectly onto the worksheet.

steps.text: Decide the size of tubing to use.

checks.text: The tubing selected matches the size, wall thickness and material called out in the applicable maintenance data.
checks.src: Handbook: "Replacement tubing should be of the same size and material as the original tubing"; procedure sheet: "Use the tubing referred to in the manual".

checks.text: Measured outside diameter of the selected stock equals the specified OD (e.g., 0.25").
checks.src: Handbook: "Metal tubing is sized by outside diameter (OD)"; the 0.25" example figure is the procedure sheet's.

checks.text: The tube's printed diameter/wall-thickness markings or alloy color band are present and legible on the selected stock.
checks.src: "The tube diameter is printed on all rigid tubing" and wall thickness "is printed on the tubing in thousandths of an inch".

checks.text: Selected alloy is appropriate to the system pressure the line will serve.
checks.src: Handbook assigns 2024-T3/5052-O/6061-T6 to "1,000 to 1,500 psi systems" and CRES to "high-pressure hydraulic systems (3,000 psi or more)".

errors.text: Tubing of correct OD but wrong alloy or thinner wall is selected, producing a line that looks correct but bursts under test pressure.
Unmarked or unidentifiable stock is used with no comparison to the original tubing's code markings.
Wrong OD stock selected, so fittings, bender channel and flare die will not match.

steps.text: Transfer length onto the tubing.

checks.text: Distance from the reference tube end to the mark equals the routed wire length plus ½" per bend.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Use a tape measure for length and add ½" per bend. This is the length of tubing you will need." Handbook gives no such figure.

checks.text: The mark is a single crisp line encircling or squarely crossing the tube, unambiguous for wheel alignment.
checks.src: Sheet requires the cutting wheel be aligned "precisely" with the marked line; handbook only speaks qualitatively of producing a square end.

checks.text: Cut length recorded on paper matches the routing measurement and bend allowance used for the mark.
checks.src: Sheet directs measuring the straightened wire and adding bend allowance; the written figure is the traceable record.

checks.text: Marked length includes surplus for bending variation, roughly 10 percent over the finished run.
checks.src: Handbook: "cut approximately 10 percent longer than the tube to be replaced to provide for minor variations in bending."

errors.text: Wire length transferred with no bend allowance, so the finished line is short after bending.
Mark made as a wide, angled or smeared band, so the cut wheel is misaligned and the flare comes out crooked.
Multiple or stale marks left on the tube, leaving the cut location ambiguous.

steps.text: Cut the tubing with a cutter tool.

checks.text: The cut end is square to the tube axis, with no angled or crooked face.
checks.src: Handbook: "it is important to produce a square end, free of burrs"; "A crooked flare is the result of the tubing not being cut squarely." Verified against a square.

checks.text: The tube at the cut is round and undeformed, with no flattening, ridging or wheel-track collapse.
checks.src: Handbook: "Too much pressure on the cutting wheel at one time could deform the tubing or cause excessive burring."

checks.text: Finished cut length equals the routed wire length plus 1/2" per bend, measured end to end.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Use a tape measure for length and add 1/2" per bend. This is the length of tubing you will need." Handbook gives no such figure.

checks.text: The cutter type used suits the tubing material (rolling cutter only for soft aluminum/copper alloy).
checks.src: Handbook: "The cutter can be used with any soft metal tubing"; "Special chipless cutters are available for cutting aluminum 6061-T6, corrosion-resistant steel, and titanium tubing."

errors.text: Tube cut off-square because the wheel wandered off the mark, yielding a crooked flare that leaks under pressure.
Cutter knob over-tightened, flattening or ovalizing the tube end and thinning the wall for flaring.
Cut made at the wrong mark, leaving the line too short to reach both fittings after bending.

steps.text: Use a single-edge deburr tool for inside diameter resizing the tubing.

checks.text: The inside edge of the tube end is smooth and free of any burr, raised lip or curl of metal.
checks.src: Procedure: "check the inside diameter is smooth"; handbook p.9-2: "carefully remove any burrs from inside and outside the tube."

checks.text: The bore at the deburred end measures the tubing's original inside diameter, not belled or enlarged.
checks.src: Procedure sheet requires "the original size returned"; handbook gives only ID calculation, no deburring tolerance.

checks.text: Wall thickness at the deburred end is not reduced or fractured relative to the printed wall thickness.
checks.src: Handbook: "use extreme care that the wall thickness of the end of the tubing is not reduced or fractured."

checks.text: No metal chips, shavings or cuttings remain inside the tube bore.
checks.src: Handbook: "Be sure all filings and cuttings are removed from the tube."

errors.text: Over-twisting the deburr tool thins or chamfers the wall, leaving a tube end that looks clean but cracks or blows off the flare under pressure.
A burr or raised lip is left inside the ID, restricting flow and able to break loose as system contamination.
Tool inserted at an angle, producing an off-center or uneven chamfer around the bore.

steps.text: Deburr the outside edge of the tubing end.

checks.text: The outside edge of the tube end is smoothly chamfered with no ragged lip, burr or sharp feathered edge.
checks.src: Handbook: "carefully remove any burrs from inside and outside the tube"; procedure sheet requires sanding "until the end is smooth".

checks.text: Wall thickness at the tube end is not reduced or fractured relative to the tube's marked wall thickness.
checks.src: Handbook: "use extreme care that the wall thickness of the end of the tubing is not reduced or fractured" — leads to defective flares.

checks.text: The tube end face is square to the tube axis, not sanded to an angle or oval.
checks.src: Handbook: "file the end square and smooth"; p.9-4 "A crooked flare is the result of the tubing not being cut squarely."

checks.text: The tube end and outer surface are free of visible metallic dust, grit and fluid smears before flaring.
checks.src: Handbook: "Be sure all filings and cuttings are removed from the tube." Sheet uses hydraulic fluid as lubricant, which traps dust.

errors.text: Excessive sanding thins or knife-edges the tube end wall, which still looks clean but cracks or blows the flare.
Tube held off-perpendicular so the end is sanded out of square, producing a crooked flare.
Metallic dust and abrasive grit left on or in the tube end, contaminating the finished line.

steps.text: Check ends for burrs.

checks.text: Both tube ends are free of burrs on the inside bore and the outside edge.
checks.src: Handbook: "carefully remove any burrs from inside and outside the tube"; procedure sheet step 3 "Check ends for burrs."

checks.text: The inside diameter is smooth and back to its original nominal size, not belled or enlarged.
checks.src: Procedure: "check the inside diameter is smooth and the original size returned"; handbook sizing by OD minus twice wall thickness.

checks.text: Wall thickness at the end is not reduced or fractured by deburring or sanding.
checks.src: Handbook: "use extreme care that the wall thickness of the end of the tubing is not reduced or fractured."

checks.text: The end face is square to the tube axis and smooth, with no nicks, scratches or gouges.
checks.src: Handbook: "produce a square end, free of burrs" and "file the end square and smooth"; squareness needs a square/gauge.

checks.text: No filings, sanding grit or metallic dust remain inside the tube after deburring.
checks.src: Handbook: "Be sure all filings and cuttings are removed from the tube"; verified by watching the tube blown/wiped clean.

errors.text: Excessive deburring thins or chamfers the end wall, leaving a plausible-looking end that will crack when flared.
Interior burr or raised lip left in the bore, becoming FOD and restricting flow while the outside looks finished.
End left out of square or with an obvious outside burr, producing a crooked flare and requiring recut.
Sanding scratches or scoring on the tube OD near the end from careless figure-8 work.

steps.text: Measure and mark where the middle of each bend will be on the tubing.

checks.text: A distinct mark is present on the tube for every bend mapped on the safety-wire template.
checks.src: Step requires a mark at each bend location; count must equal bends recorded during routing.

checks.text: Each mark's distance from the reference tube end matches the corresponding wire-template dimension.
checks.src: Senior note: 'Measure from the ends of the wire to the bend marks. Use that dimension to mark on the tubing.'

checks.text: Marks are felt-tip only, with no scribe lines, scratches or dents in the tube wall.
checks.src: Sheet lists felt tip marker; handbook: tubing 'must be free from cracks, dents, nicks, scratches, or any other defects.'

checks.text: Mark count and spacing agree with the routing sketch/photo of the bent wire.
checks.src: Routing note 2: 'Draw or photograph the shape to make' — the sketch is the reference for verification.

errors.text: Dimensions transferred from the wrong wire end, mirroring bend locations on the tube.
Mark scribed or scratched into the tube instead of marked, creating a stress riser.
Mark placed at the start of the bend rather than its middle, offsetting every bend.
Mark too wide or smeared to align precisely with the bender L/R line.

steps.text: Use a hand bender to bend the tubing.

checks.text: The finished bend is smooth and free of kinks, wrinkles, or visible flat spots.
checks.src: Handbook: "Bend the tubing carefully to avoid excessive flattening, kinking, or wrinkling"; "Tubing with flattened, wrinkled, or irregular bends should not be installed."

checks.text: The small diameter of any flattened portion of the bend is at least 75 percent of the original tube OD.
checks.src: Handbook: "the small diameter of the flattened portion must not be less than 75 percent of the original outside diameter."

checks.text: The completed bend angle matches the angle called for by the routing template.
checks.src: Handbook: "pull the form handle until the zero mark on the form handle lines up with the desired angle of bend"; sheet: "until the upper handle 0 points to the desired degrees."

checks.text: The bend center falls at the marked location, measured from the correct (L or R) reference end.
checks.src: Handbook: "align the mark on the tubing with the L on the form handle... If the measured end is on the right side, then align... with the R."

errors.text: Bend is flattened close to or below the 75 percent OD limit while still appearing acceptable to a novice.
Bend is kinked or wrinkled from wrong-size bender channel or jerky handle motion, requiring the tube be scrapped.
L/R reference reversed or zeros not aligned, placing the bend at the wrong distance or angle from the measured end.

steps.text: Repeat at each marked bend location.

checks.text: Every marked bend location on the tube has a corresponding formed bend, matching the count and sequence of the wire template.

checks.text: Each bend is smooth and free of wrinkles, kinks, or visible flattening.
checks.src: Handbook: 'Tubing with flattened, wrinkled, or irregular bends should not be installed'; procedure sheet requires smooth bender-formed bends.

checks.text: At each bend the small diameter of any flattened portion is not less than 75 percent of the original outside diameter.
checks.src: Handbook: 'the small diameter of the flattened portion must not be less than 75 percent of the original outside diameter'.

checks.text: Bend angles and the distances between bends reproduce the wire-template dimensions within fit-up of both fittings.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Measure from the ends of the wire to the bend marks. Use that dimension to mark on the tubing.'

errors.text: A subsequent bend is formed off the L/R reference or in the wrong plane, so the line will not seat in both fittings.

Over-bent joint is bent back or re-worked, work-hardening the tube and producing a kink or wrinkle.

steps.text: Install the hardware.

checks.text: The B-nut is on the tube with its threaded end facing the tube end to be flared.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Slide the B-nut on the tube with the threads pointing towards the end being flared." Handbook only says slip nut on tube.

checks.text: The sleeve sits between the B-nut and the tube end with its larger opening facing that end.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Slide the sleeve on with the larger opening pointing towards the end of the tube being flared." Handbook is silent on orientation.

checks.text: Both nut and sleeve are on the tube while the end is still square and unflared.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-4: "Cut the tube squarely and remove all burrs. Slip the fitting nut and sleeve on the tube." Sequence precedes flaring in both sources.

checks.text: Nut and sleeve size matches the tube outside diameter and both slide freely on the tube.
checks.src: Procedure sheet specifies tubing per manual (e.g. 0.25" OD) with matching B-nut and sleeve; fit verified by measuring OD against hardware.

errors.text: Sleeve installed reversed, small opening toward the flare, so it cannot support the flare face.
Flare formed before hardware installed, requiring the flare to be cut off and remade.
B-nut installed with threads facing away from the end being flared.

steps.text: Use the flaring tool.

checks.text: The finished flare is concentric and square to the tube axis, not lopsided or crooked.
checks.src: Handbook: "A crooked flare is the result of the tubing not being cut squarely"; procedure sheet: "holder is square to the tube."

checks.text: Flare face and adjacent tube surface are free of cracks, splits, nicks, scratches or die scoring.
checks.src: Handbook: "The flare and tubing must be free from cracks, dents, nicks, scratches, or any other defects"; sheet warns of scoring.

checks.text: Flare outside diameter is neither undersized nor oversized for the sleeve and B-nut thread engagement.
checks.src: "A flare made too small produces a weak joint... if made too large, it interferes with the proper engagement of the screw thread"; handbook gives no figure.

checks.text: Flare angle matches the taught 47° die form, not an automotive 45° flare.
checks.src: Procedure sheet states "a good 47° flare"; the angle figure comes from the sheet only and needs gauge or comparator reading.

checks.text: Tube protruded about a dime's thickness through the tapered die and the anvil was run in until torque rose and the die seated.
checks.src: Sheet: extend "about the thickness of a dime" and rotate "until a noticeable rise in torque is felt." Setup and feel are not visible afterward.

errors.text: Tube under-flared (anvil not seated), leaving a thick sleeve ring that can blow off under pressure while looking finished.
Over-flared end thinned or cracked at the rim, which will leak or fail when pressurized.
Tube clamped at an angle, producing a crooked, one-sided flare that will not seat in the fitting.
Die jaws score or mar the tube wall behind the flare from loose or angled clamping.

steps.text: Check for a good flare.

checks.text: With the sleeve pulled up against the flare, a thin, continuous ring of the blue sleeve is visible around the flared end.
checks.src: Procedure sheet's go/no-go check: thin blue ring = correct flare size; thick ring = under-flared, no ring = over-flared.

checks.text: The flare and adjacent tubing are free of cracks, splits, dents, nicks, scratches or scoring from the die.
checks.src: Handbook: "The flare and tubing must be free from cracks, dents, nicks, scratches, or any other defects." Sheet warns scoring causes failure under pressure.

checks.text: The flare is concentric and square to the tube axis, not crooked or lopsided in wall thickness.
checks.src: Handbook: "A crooked flare is the result of the tubing not being cut squarely"; flare must be "properly shaped or the connection leaks or fails."

checks.text: The included flare angle measures 47° per the procedure sheet (handbook specifies 35° to 37°).
checks.src: Angle figure 47° is the procedure sheet's alone; handbook states dies "ground to produce a flare of 35° to 37°." Requires gauge, not a photo.

errors.text: Under-flared end (thick blue sleeve ring showing) accepted as good; may blow off under system pressure.
Over-flared end (no sleeve ring visible) accepted; flare cracks under pressure and leaks.
Flare scored, split or thinned from angled/over-tightened die insertion but passed on visual glance.

steps.text: Repeat hardware and flare process for the other end.

checks.text: Both tube ends carry a completed flare, with a B-nut and sleeve captured on the tube for each end.
checks.src: Sheet: slide B-nut with threads toward the end being flared and sleeve with larger opening toward that end, then repeat for other end.

checks.text: On each end the B-nut threads and the sleeve's larger opening face their own flare, not each other.
checks.src: Hardware orientation per Senior Mechanic Note 1; reversed hardware cannot seat on the flare.

checks.text: The second flare is concentric and square to the tube axis and free of cracks, nicks, scratches or splits.
checks.src: Handbook: "The flare and tubing must be free from cracks, dents, nicks, scratches, or any other defects"; "A crooked flare is the result of the tubing not being cut squarely."

checks.text: The second flare's included angle matches the specified flare angle for the fitting.
checks.src: Sheet specifies a 47° flare; handbook states dies "produce a flare of 35° to 37°" and forbids 45° automotive flares.

errors.text: Sleeve or B-nut installed backwards, or omitted, before flaring the second end.

steps.text: Use an enclosed pressure test box.

checks.text: The entire fabricated line, including both end fittings, sits inside the test box with nothing protruding past the enclosure walls.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: 'Use an enclosed pressure test box'; safety note warns high-pressure fluid sprayed at the body causes severe injury.

checks.text: The box lid or door is fully closed and latched before any pressure is applied to the line.
checks.src: Containment only exists while closed; a still of a closed box cannot show whether the line was inside or when pressure began.

checks.text: The enclosure and its viewing panel are intact, with no cracks, missing panels or open gaps facing the operator.
checks.src: Enclosure is the sole spray barrier implied by 'enclosed pressure test box' and the high-pressure spray hazard note.

checks.text: The box is rated for at least the intended test pressure of 1.5 times system pressure.
checks.src: Procedure sheet sets test pressure at 1.5x system (e.g. 3000 psi); enclosure rating must be confirmed from shop equipment data.

errors.text: Line pressurized with the box open or with a fitting left outside the enclosure, so a burst sprays the operator.
Test hose routed over the lip so the lid cannot close, leaving a gap aimed at the work area.
Line laid in the box resting on a bend or fitting instead of supported, risking movement during pressurization.

steps.text: Connect the completed rigid line to the pressure tester pump.

checks.text: The B-nut is fully run down square on the tester port with no visible thread gap or cross-threading.
checks.src: Step requires the completed line connected to the pump; full square engagement is the inspectable outcome of that connection.

checks.text: Two wrenches are used simultaneously, one holding the tester fitting stationary so no twist reaches the tube or flare.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note: 'Use two wrenches when connecting the rigid line to the tester.' Only observable while turning.

checks.text: The two wrenches are set about 45° apart on the hardware and squeezed together like plier handles.
checks.src: Procedure sheet alone specifies 45°; handbook pp.9-1..9-7 give no wrench-positioning figure.

checks.text: Final tightness is reached at a firm torque rise, not by adding torque in an attempt to seal a poor flare.
checks.src: Handbook: 'If a flare is not made properly, flaws cannot be corrected by applying additional torque when tightening the fitting.'

errors.text: Single wrench used, twisting the tube and distorting or cracking the flare while the joint still looks correctly assembled.
Over-tightening the B-nut to stop a weep instead of re-making a defective flare.
B-nut cross-threaded or only partially engaged on the tester port.

steps.text: Place the rigid line into the enclosed box.

checks.text: The entire tube assembly, including both B-nut/fitting connections, lies wholly inside the enclosure with nothing protruding past the box opening.
checks.src: Procedure sheet requires an enclosed pressure test box and the line placed into it; cited handbook pages state no enclosure requirement.

checks.text: The box cover/closure is fully seated and latched, with only the supply hose passing through its intended port.
checks.src: Containment of high-pressure fluid; sheet warns 'High pressure fluids can cause severe injuries if sprayed at body.'

checks.text: The line shows no new kink, flat spot or wrinkle from being forced or sprung into the box.
checks.src: Handbook: 'Tubing with flattened, wrinkled, or irregular bends should not be installed'; flattening limit itself needs measurement.

checks.text: The box is closed and all personnel are clear of the spray path before any pumping begins.
checks.src: Sequencing and personnel position; sheet lists high-pressure spray injury and eye/mouth exposure hazards.

errors.text: Line pressurized with the box lid open or with a fitting end hanging outside the enclosure.
Assembly sprung or bent to fit the box, kinking or flattening a bend or straining a flare.
Loose rags, tools or FOD left in the box with the line, or fluid drips not wiped up.

steps.text: Pressurize the rigid line.

checks.text: The test gauge reaches 1.5 times the documented system operating pressure (e.g., 3,000 psi for a 2,000 psi system).
checks.src: Procedure sheet alone gives the 1.5x figure; handbook only says tubing is "designed to withstand several times the normal operating pressure."

checks.text: The system operating pressure used to compute test pressure is traceable to the aircraft manual/TCDS for the installation.
checks.src: Sheet requires use of all relevant data (TCDS, maintenance/service manuals) to establish system pressure.

checks.text: Indicated pressure holds at test value without decay for the observation period.
checks.src: Pressurization exists to reveal leaks; a falling gauge indicates leakage at b-nut, sleeve or tube.

checks.text: Pressure is applied only with the line inside the enclosed test box and personnel clear of the line.
checks.src: Sheet requires an enclosed pressure test box; safety note: "High pressure fluids can cause severe injuries if sprayed at body."

errors.text: Line pressurized to system pressure only, not 1.5x, so a weak flare passes an inadequate test.
Pressure applied with the enclosure open or body/hands near the line, exposing personnel to high-pressure spray.
Pump run well past the calculated test pressure, yielding or bulging the tube and requiring refabrication.

steps.text: Check tubing for leaks.

checks.text: The line holds the specified test pressure with no gauge decay during the leak check.
checks.src: Procedure sheet alone gives 1.5× system pressure (e.g. 3,000 psi for a 2,000 psi system); handbook only says tubing is pressure tested and withstands several times normal pressure.

checks.text: No fluid seepage appears at either B-nut or at the base of either sleeve while the line is pressurized.
checks.src: Procedure sheet ties leak location to fault; handbook p.9-4: "the flare on the tubing must be properly shaped or the connection leaks or fails."

checks.text: No weeping, misting or wetness appears along the tube body or through the bend under pressure.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Leak on tubing = possible damage from fabrication"; handbook p.9-1 requires tubing be pressure tested prior to installation.

checks.text: Joints and tube are wiped dry and free of residual fluid before the pressure check begins.
checks.src: Leak-location diagnosis in the senior mechanic notes is only valid if pre-existing fluid is removed first.

errors.text: A leak at the sleeve base is 'fixed' by further tightening the B-nut instead of re-flaring the tube.
Line inspected only after depressurizing or after wiping, so a slow weep is never observed and the line is passed.
Leak check performed below the 1.5× test pressure, so a marginal flare or joint is not challenged.

steps.text: Fit rigid line into position.

checks.text: Both tube ends align concentrically with their fitting seats, with no visible offset or gap when set in place.
checks.src: Procedure step 'Fit rigid line into position' before tightening; misalignment forces the flare off its seat.

checks.text: The line shows no flattened, wrinkled, kinked or irregular bends anywhere along its length.
checks.src: Handbook: "Tubing with flattened, wrinkled, or irregular bends should not be installed."

checks.text: Any flattening at a bend measures not less than 75 percent of the original tube outside diameter.
checks.src: Handbook: "the small diameter of the flattened portion must not be less than 75 percent of the original outside diameter."

checks.text: Flares and tube surfaces are free of cracks, dents, nicks and scratches where fitted.
checks.src: Handbook: "The flare and tubing must be free from cracks, dents, nicks, scratches, or any other defects."

checks.text: The fitted line clears adjacent structure and components with no contact or chafing point.
checks.src: Routing was mapped to avoid obstructions; fit must reproduce that clearance.

errors.text: Line is sprung or pulled into the fittings, pre-loading the flare and risking cross-threaded b-nuts.
A line with a flattened or kinked bend is fitted anyway, inviting fatigue failure in service.
Line rests against or bears on adjacent structure, creating a chafe point.

steps.text: Tighten rigid line on fittings.

checks.text: Each b-nut is run up square and fully engaged on its fitting, with no cocked nut, cross-threading, or unengaged exposed threads.
checks.src: Handbook speaks only qualitatively of "proper engagement of the screw thread on the fitting"; squareness/engagement judgement is the sheet's.

checks.text: Final tightening on each b-nut is the point of high torque rise plus one-third turn, no more and no less.
checks.src: The ⅓-turn figure appears only on the procedure sheet; the handbook gives no turn value for flared b-nut installation.

checks.text: A backup wrench holds the fitting while the b-nut is turned, so no torque reaches the tube or the airframe fitting.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note: two wrenches, one on b-nut and one on fitting.

checks.text: No extra torque beyond the specified tightening is used to stop a weep or to seat an imperfect flare.
checks.src: Handbook: "If a flare is not made properly, flaws cannot be corrected by applying additional torque when tightening the fitting."

errors.text: B-nut over-torqued well past the ⅓ turn, shearing or cracking the flare while the joint still looks correctly assembled.
Tightened with a single wrench, rotating the fitting or twisting the tube and preloading the installed line.
B-nut cross-threaded or left cocked on the fitting, with visible thread gap.
Wrench marks, rounded flats, or galling on the b-nut and fitting hex.
